The legacy Matlab \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{randraw.m}} surface has been retired. Probability distributions now live in the C++ API as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}, available directly from:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is organized around how users actually consume the layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quickstart}} for the short\sphinxhyphen{}path workflow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{api\_reference}} when you need the function surface

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distribution\_catalog}} when you need names, aliases, and parameter conventions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build\_outputs}} when you want to build the docs or the example binary locally

\end{itemize}

\label{\detokenize{quickstart:quickstart}}\label{\detokenize{quickstart::doc}}

\section{Include Path}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:include-path}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distribution layer is exposed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}. No extra include is needed when PlussMa is part of the build.

\section{Intended Style}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:intended-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user\sphinxhyphen{}facing model is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keep everything under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pass the distribution name plus a short parameter list

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
let \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like}} carry shape and dtype when you already have a target tensor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stay on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throughout instead of bouncing between helper wrappers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{API Reference}
\label{\detokenize{api_reference:api-reference}}\label{\detokenize{api_reference::doc}}

\section{Entry Point}
\label{\detokenize{api_reference:entry-point}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All distribution functionality is available from:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{distr}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
That alias resolves to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::subsp::stat::distr}}, but user code should generally prefer the shorter public path.


\section{Core Functions}
\label{\detokenize{api_reference:core-functions}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
zero\sphinxhyphen{}parameter distributions via \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample(name, sizes, cfg, seed)}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\section{Parameter Conventions}
\label{\detokenize{distribution_catalog:parameter-conventions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Selected conventions carried over from the legacy surface:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{beta}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}a, b{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}m, n, a, b{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gamma}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}a{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}m, b, a{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}nu{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}nu, chi, eta{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chi}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}nu{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}a, b, nu{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{weibull}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}shape, scale{]}}} or legacy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}theta, alpha, beta{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normaltrunc}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}a, b, mu, sigma{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hypergeom}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}N, M, n{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nig}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}alpha, beta, mu, delta{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gh}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}lambda, alpha, beta, mu, delta{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gig}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}lambda, chi, psi{]}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When in doubt, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr::supports(name)}} first and then keep the parameter list minimal.
